extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory familiar with Inter-Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and proof of explicit diophantine (ABC/Vojta-type) inequalities within Mochizuki's IUT framework, including construction of initial Θ-data and local-to-global upper bound computations. Intended for researchers following IUTch series.

rubrics_metrics.name: assume l is large (l ≥ 5, sometimes l ≥ 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The argument requires taking l to be 'large'; various displayed inequalities and estimates apply under hypotheses such as 'l ≥ 5' and in some places 'l ≥ 7'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly to simplify/estimate coefficient factors (e.g., to apply estimates like (l+1)/4 ≤ 20/3 etc.) and to ensure validity of bounds; the text explicitly notes 'When l is sufficiently large' and uses l ≥ 5 (and occasionally l ≥ 7) to justify numerical inequalities in the proof of Theorem 1.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: exclude primes over 2 from Vbad_mod
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonarchimedean primes of even residue characteristic where the elliptic curve has bad multiplicative reduction are excluded from Vbad_mod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification: the etale-theta-function theory ([EtTh]) fails at p=2 (special value becomes a non-unit when p=2), which breaks multiradiality needed for cyclotomic and constant-multiple rigidity. Thus the construction and estimates require excluding such primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: work over the field of rationality of l-torsion points (use K not F)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is crucial to work over the field of rationality of the l-torsion points (i.e., K rather than F) when considering global and local ΘNF- and Θ±ell-Hodge theaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids Galois indeterminacy in l-torsion points which would invalidate delicate manipulations involving l-torsion points used elsewhere (e.g., Propositions in IUTchI).

rubrics_metrics.name: initial Θ-data — choose X = P1, D = {0,1,∞}, and suitable KV
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of Suitable Initial Θ-Data: take X = P1_Q, D = {0,1,∞} (the λ-line) and choose KV ⊆ UX(Q) a compactly bounded subset whose support contains the nonarchimedean prime 2 and which satisfies condition (*j-inv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition (*j-inv): for the nonarchimedean prime v = 2, the image of the associated Kv ⊆ UX(Q_v) via the j-invariant is bounded in A1(Q_v) of the form 2^{N_{j-inv}}·O_{Q_v}. This concrete hypothesis on KV is part of the data needed to apply the subsequent Diophantine conclusions (Corollary 2.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: use Prime Number Theorem quantitative bound (existence of ξ_prm ≥ 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists ξ_prm ≥ 5 such that for real x ≥ ξ_prm, θ(x) = ∑_{p ≤ x} log(p) satisfies x/ (3/2) ≤ θ(x) ≤ (4/3) x (text phrasing: 'there exists a real number ξprm ≥ 5 such that ...  (2/3) · x ≤ θ(x) ≤ (4/3) · x').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to control sums over primes and to deduce existence of a prime p ∈ A with p ≤ 2(θ_A + ξ_prm) for a finite set A of primes. This PNT bound is invoked in Proposition 2.1 and used to bound log(s≤) and related prime sums in Step (viii) and numerical estimations.

rubrics_metrics.name: apply Proposition 1.4 with explicit identifications (for vQ ∈ Vdst)
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply Proposition 1.4 (iii) in the vQ ∈ Vdst case, set I = S±_{j+1}, I* = {i ∈ I : e_v_i > p_{vQ}-2} (or similar), k_i = K_{v_i} (so R_i = O_{K_{v_i}}), i† = j ∈ S±_{j+1}, and choose λ = 0 if v_j ∈ Vgood and λ = ord(−) of q_{j^2_{v_j}} if v_j ∈ Vbad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With these assignments the inclusion φ(p^λ · (R_I)~) ⊆ p^{λ-d_I-a_I} · log_p(R_I^×) from Proposition 1.4(iii) is used to bound the images of Θ-pilot objects and thereby produce upper bounds for components of log-volume. The text gives the explicit mapping and then derives resulting inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: handle indeterminacies Ind1, Ind2 by automorphism φ and Ind3 by upper bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeterminacies (Ind1) and (Ind2) are taken into account by the arbitrary nature of the automorphism φ (cf. Proposition 1.2), while Ind3 is handled by considering upper bounds and suitable integer powers of p_{vQ}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a prescriptive methodological requirement: when forming containers for 'possible images of a Θ-pilot object' one must account for these three indeterminacies in the stated manner; the text repeatedly uses this principle in Steps (iv)–(vii).

rubrics_metrics.name: symmetrize over choice of i† for weighted averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Because 'λ' is asymmetric with respect to the choice of i† ∈ I in S±_{j+1}, the argument requires symmetrizing with respect to i† when computing weighted averages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The operation of symmetrization is shown not to affect the computation of the weighted-average upper bound (by Proposition 1.7); this is a procedural step when moving from local component bounds to averaged/normalized global bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: vQ ∈ Vnon case: apply Proposition 1.4(iv) to obtain bound 0
rubrics_metrics.description: When vQ ∈ Vnon the hypotheses of Proposition 1.4(iv) are satisfied and the inclusion φ((R_I)~) ⊆ (R_I)~ implies the tensor product of log-shells contains the 'union of possible images', leading to a log-volume bound equal to 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies a local situation where the procession-normalized upper bound vanishes; the text prescribes applying Prop.1.4(iv) and then performing the same averaging/normalization steps as in other local cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: vQ ∈ Varc case: apply Proposition 1.5(iii),(iv) with chosen π_{j+1}
rubrics_metrics.description: For vQ ∈ Varc set I = S±_{j+1}, V = V(F_mod)_{vQ}, C_v = K_v (with v corresponding appropriately), and choose factor π_{j+1} so that π_{j+1}·B_I contains the union of possible images; the log-volume of B_I is normalized to 0 leading to bounds like (j+1)·log(π) and a procession-normalized bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a concrete recipe for producing the local container and associated log-volume estimate in the Varc case; the text uses normalizations tied to arithmetic degrees to set the log-volume of B_I to 0 and then computes the ensuing global normalized bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: compute procession-normalized upper bound by averaging over j ∈ F_l
rubrics_metrics.description: After obtaining weighted-average upper bounds at fixed j, one must average over j ∈ {1,...,l-1} (i.e., j ∈ F_l) and apply combinatorial/estimate steps (E1),(E2) to obtain the 'procession-normalized upper bound' used in Theorem 1.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives explicit averaged expressions and inequalities (leading to the final bounds in Theorem 1.10); this is the prescribed procedure to pass from local per-j bounds to the global bound C_Θ.

rubrics_metrics.name: use estimate bounds for log(s≤) via Proposition 1.6 and ξ_prm
rubrics_metrics.description: To bound terms like l*_mod · log(s≤) one applies Proposition 1.6 and the prime-sum estimates: when e*_mod · l ≥ η_prm sum over p ≤ e*_mod · l and otherwise bound by η_prm-related constant; uniformly obtain l*_mod · log(s≤) ≤ (4/3)(e*_mod · l + η_prm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This numeric control is used to absorb terms into coarse bounds (e.g., to show l*_mod·log(s≤) ≤ 4/3·(e*_mod·l + η_prm) and then dominate by constants for final Theorem 1.10 numeric estimate).

rubrics_metrics.name: simplifying assumption for computational discussion: F_tpd = Q (so d_mod = 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For asymptotic and computational discussion, one may assume F_tpd = Q, which forces d_mod = 1 and simplifies notation (δ := log(d_Ftpd) + log(f_Ftpd) = log(f_Ftpd)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an optional simplifying hypothesis used in Remark 1.10.5(ii) to discuss asymptotic behavior of the bounds and leading terms; the text explains consequences for the behavior of the '(cid:2) terms'.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid Galois indeterminacy in l-torsion points
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow Galois indeterminacy with respect to l-torsion points in local portions (prime-strips) — i.e., work relative to field K of rationality of l-torsion points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such indeterminacy were allowed even at places in V_non, it would invalidate delicate l-torsion manipulations in IUTchI §4, §6 (Propositions 4.7, 6.5). This is a methodological constraint on allowed data.
